messages:
michael (eng-infra): heads up — we're getting a burst of 429/placement failures for a Dedicated tenant (acct-431) in us-east-2. autoscaler isn't launching new GPU nodes in az-b, seems az imbalance. seeing placement_error: insufficient_gpu_in_az

sophia (oncall): confirmed alerts at 12:14 UTC. p95 latency +5%, some streaming inits 502/timeout. sample alloc log below:
```
[2026-02-28T12:13:47Z] alloc request_id=req-9f3 tenant=acct-431 region=us-east-2 az=az-b placement_error=insufficient_gpu_in_az
[2026-02-28T12:13:48Z] autoscaler decision: avoid_az=az-b reason=soft_cap_reached
[2026-02-28T12:14:03Z] api response 429 for req-9f3
```

kai (support): customer pinged support — they see repeated 429s and a billing line that shows a provisioning attempt but no capacity. ticket CS-983 is high-priority. they want ETA and workaround.

jessica (account): which customers affected besides acct-431? any SLA breaches yet? need a short note for them.

michael (eng-infra): only acct-431 so far on Dedicated pools in us-east-2. Cause hypothesis: per-AZ GPU quotas are hit in az-b but region has free capacity in az-a/c, autoscaler policy is too strict about AZ balancing; when az-b hits soft cap, placement logic spins waiting for az-b to free up instead of falling back to az-a. Also saw a cloud provider 400 on instance create with message: `attachment_failure: insufficient_pv_in_az`.

sophia (oncall): repro steps I used locally:
```
# simulate dedicated alloc for problematic tenant
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/dedicated/alloc \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -d '{"tenant":"acct-431","model":"rwi-medium","region":"us-east-2","preferred_az":"az-b"}'
# returns
{"error":"placement_failure","reason":"az_capacity_quota"}
```

sam (eng-platform): looks like two things: 1) noisy neighbor with long-running batch job pinned to az-b consuming fractionated GPUs, 2) autoscaler AZ-balancer heuristics preventing cross-az fallback. I'll push a small change to relax AZ affinity for Dedicated pools as a temporary mitigation.

deploy-bot: deploy started by sam: `eng-platform/az-affinity-relax v1.2.3`

michael (eng-infra): temporary mitigations we can do now: 1) manual scale-up: add +4 GPUs to the dedicated pool in us-east-2 az-a via controlplane UI (quickest), 2) force-failover tenant to us-east-1 for next 30m using `alloc.override_region`, 3) increase per-AZ soft cap threshold from 0.8 -> 0.95 in autoscaler config (riskier).

kai (support): shared workaround with customer: set `preferred_region=us-east-1` in their API calls OR we can initiate failover for them. they asked about billing: are failed provisioning attempts billed? we should confirm.

sophia (oncall): observation: noisy-tenant id nt-19 has 12 long-lived allocations pinned to az-b (large-batch). Proposed quick action: evict non-critical low-priority allocations in az-b for next 15m to free slots. Anyone object? :warning:

jessica (account): customer prefers not to be moved without notice. if we force failover we should provide clear timelines and credit offer. I'll draft message once we have ETA.

sam (eng-platform): patch rolled out to relax AZ affinity (can fallback to other AZs within region). monitoring it now. If that doesn't free things, I'll trigger manual bootstrap of 4 GPUs in az-a. ETA for monitoring: 5–10m.

michael (eng-infra): added temporary rate-limit override for acct-431 to reduce retry storms (set to 50 rps). also set fallback-model policy to allow `rwi-small` if `rwi-medium` can't be placed.

sophia (oncall): current numbers: 429 count down from 780/min -> 120/min after mod, p95 latency trending down. still seeing a handful of placement_failure logs.

kai (support): customer updated — they see improvement. keep me posted before we close CS-983.

jessica (account): great. hold on message to customers until we confirm stable for 30m. I will include credit offer language.

michael (eng-infra): postmortem checklist for follow-up: 1) increase observability on per-AZ fragmentation metrics, 2) tune autoscaler AZ fallback policy, 3) introduce noisy-tenant isolation for long-running batch jobs, 4) verify billing behavior for failed provisioning attempts and update docs. Owners: sam(autoscaler), sophia(oncall followup), michael(infra + billing check), jessica(customer comms).

sophia (oncall): marking incident mitigated at 12:52 UTC — traffic mostly healthy, continuing to monitor for 1h. :white_check_mark:
